text:
Priya: pinging eng oncall — customer AcmeHealth (dedicated pool eu-west-1) reporting repeated 429s and 1.5-2s P99 for /v1/generate. They say autoscaler didn't add capacity for ~7m despite sustained queue.
Leo: on it. Can you paste the customer request id or example request timestamps? Also which pool (pool-id) are they on?
Priya: request ids: req_20260315_2312_a1, req_20260315_2319_b4. Pool: dedicated-euwh-002. They said traffic ramped from ~80 rps to ~200 rps around 23:12 UTC and stayed high.
Oncall Bot: auto-ack — paging oncall.
Sam: quick check — what does the HPA / autoscaler think the desired replicas were? Any recent config changes to min/max or scale policy?
Priya: support checked with customer: minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=12. No config changes from their side. They attached a small graph from the console showing CPU & queue length.
Leo: pulling metrics now. From control plane: between 23:12 and 23:19 avg queue depth per replica went from 0.4 -> 3.8. Targets show desired_replicas stayed at 2 until 23:19, then jumped to 6 at 23:20. That's ~8 minutes of under-provision. Looking at scale policy: scaleUp.cooldownSeconds=300, scaleUp.step=+1 per evaluation with eval interval 30s. That explains slower ramp (stepwise +1).
Kevin: ugh, step=+1 and cooldown 300s is aggressive for bursty customer traffic. Did the autoscaler hit any API rate limits or backoff from provider? Check controller logs.
Leo: grabbing controller logs. Found repeated `scale request rejected` lines due to topology constraint: "insufficient GPU capacity in eu-west-1b for requested instance type". So the control plane attempted to create a new node but provider returned capacity errors — autoscaler retried, kept step upping slowly but some attempts failed. Logs pasted below:

```
[2026-03-15T23:13:02Z] scale-controller: desired=3 -> request nodePool=create-spot-euwest1b count=1
[2026-03-15T23:13:07Z] cloud-provider: CreateInstance failed: InsufficientCapacity: no matching GPU in zone eu-west-1b
[2026-03-15T23:14:02Z] scale-controller: desired=3 -> requeue
[2026-03-15T23:18:55Z] scale-controller: desired=4 -> request nodePool=create-ondemand-euwest1a count=1
[2026-03-15T23:19:20Z] cloud-provider: CreateInstance succeeded: node-abc123
```

Leo: so two issues: (1) policy step size + long cooldown made scaling slow in normal conditions; (2) cloud capacity errors caused additional delays.
Priya: customer says they still got 429s even after new nodes came up. Any warmup (cold start) delays on model runner? How long to join pool and become ready?
Sam: model startup time for their pinned model ~45-70s cold start for GPU provisioning + model load + warming KV. We have feature "fast-warm" disabled for this pool (costly). That adds ~1m. Combining provider spin up + model load yields the observed ~2-3m lag in best case; capacity failures extended that to ~8m.
Kevin: can you share exact repro steps? We'll try to reproduce with a load test in a staging pool with same scale params.
Priya: repro steps provided to customer and staging:
1) Pin a heavy model (resnet-xx-large) to pool dedicated-euwh-002
2) Start steady 80 rps for 10m
3) At t=0, ramp to 200 rps (sustained) using simple curl worker: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST \"https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"input": "lorem"}' & done`
4) Observe errors/429s and replica counts for 10m
Sam: thanks. I'll run the same in staging with pool config min=2 max=12 scale.step=+1 cooldown=300s and a simulated reduced zone capacity to mimic InsufficientCapacity responses.
Leo: short-term mitigations for production customer:
- Bump minReplicas to 4 for this customer's pool to give headroom (support action after customer approval)
- Temporarily enable fast-warm for their pool for next 24h
- Add fallback route to regional replica pool (lower-cost model variant) if scale fails
Priya: customer approved bump to minReplicas=4 and fast-warm for 2h window. I've scheduled this change for 23:45 UTC. Also created ticket SUP-8734 for billing/approval notes.
Oncall Bot: action recorded: SUP-8734 assigned to Support (Priya). Escalation ENG-1129 opened to Infra for autoscaler policy review.
Kevin: long-term: infra should consider changing scale.up.step to a percent-based increase (e.g., +50% or +2) or allow burst pool that can spin up pre-warmed instances. Also add detection when cloud returns InsufficientCapacity and automatically try alternate zones/types quickly.
Leo: agreed — will add a short RFC to eng-infra with logs and metrics. For now, I'll monitor the customer's pool during the next 60m and post metrics.
Priya: monitoring: after minReplicas bump and fast-warm toggle at 23:45, request queue drains in ~70s and 429s stop. Customer confirms degraded UX fixed. Will follow up with postmortem and recommended config defaults for similar customers.
Sam: thanks team. Next steps: (1) postmortem draft (SUP-8734 + ENG-1129) (2) run staging repro and propose autoscaler policy changes (3) implement fallback routing check during scale failures.
Kevin: :thumbsup: please tag me on the RFC.
Priya: will do. Closing thread for now, will post links to tickets and graphs in the postmortem.
